status: Read-only preparation; not implemented. Source ownership remains with the current gate implementer. SNAPSHOT starts only after GATE-REVIEWS.

protocol.observation: Return snapshot_schema=2, observation_token={epoch,generation}, the small original model/inspector fields (url,title,w,h,text,scroll,actions,evidence,omitted_actions), and bounded action guard references. Do not transmit marker/page_key/large target guards.
protocol.observe: Scan into local prospective values. Allocate a provisional next-generation token. Construct and measure the complete public response. Only a successful below-ceiling observation atomically replaces the latest baseline, guard table and retained target map. Every successful observe advances generation, including an unchanged page.
protocol.fresh: Use a dedicated cached comparison function receiving schema/token and optional action/guard reference. Never invoke observe or READ_STATE through the old MARKER expression. Reject absent/recreated cache, wrong document/epoch/generation, unrecognized target or stale guard reference. Scanning may allocate weak IDs for newly seen nodes, but must not replace the baseline, token or strong target map.
protocol.baseline: Keep only the latest accepted exact global semantics, exact page/form key, per-target guard records and deduplicated scope strings. Equality compares full arrays/strings; JSON serialization equality is acceptable, semantic hashes or mutation counters are not.
protocol.scoped_vs_global: Global freshness retains current full marker semantics. CLICK/SELECT scoped freshness retains page/form key plus selected target/scope guard semantics; do not silently substitute progress data or overclaim broader guarantees. Continue current geometry exclusion for freshness and perform hit-testing at execution.
protocol.select: Replace transported page_key/guard in SELECT_ACTION with the page token and a target guard reference tied to epoch+generation+node. In the same synchronous evaluation, validate token/reference, recompute exact applicable evidence, check the existing select/option descriptor and current geometry, then selectedIndex and one event pair. No await or retry. Explicit overflow before assignment must raise SnapshotTooLarge, not UncertainAction or StalePage.
protocol.schema_compatibility: Old stored observations remain data for readers. Browser freshness/execution must not accept a missing schema, old schema, replayed serialized token or references from another session. Never add an implicit legacy execution fallback.

progress.keep: URL, visible text, capped actions with geometry, scroll position and height, plus the SELECT-stage multi-select evidence. Use the complete canonical observation before policy filtering. Preserve semantic option identity/index/label/value/state.
progress.exclude: All added protocol identity wherever nested: schema version, observation token, guard reference/generation, document_id, cache_epoch and diagnostic work counters. Current descriptor document/cache exclusions must be extended to nested references rather than replaced by dropping the descriptor.
parity_cases: Unchanged observe twice: different observation token, equal progress fingerprint; first token is stale.
Freshness A -> mutate B -> check old token twice: false both times; baseline remains A.
Geometry-only movement within viewport: unchanged freshness; changed progress because rect is retained.
Scroll-height-only change: changed progress, with freshness behavior matching baseline.
Offscreen form property or omitted control semantics change: global freshness false; unchanged progress when capped actions/text/scroll are unchanged.
Title-only change: global freshness false, progress unchanged if its established projection is unchanged.
Changed multi-select selected values: evidence/progress changes; no SELECT or descendant CLICK becomes eligible.

bounded_work.two_pass: Continue the complete semantic scan, including omitted candidates and safe offscreen form properties. Retain only first250 target actions for public eligibility before building target guards. Scroll/WAIT controls remain separate from the250 target-action cap.
bounded_work.identity: identity(node) updates only WeakMap identity allocation. A separate retain(node) builds the new strong reverse map for offered controls and offered SELECT options. Observation-only multiple controls and global signature nodes need scalar/weak identity only.
bounded_work.scope: Read scope.innerText once per distinct target scope per scan and retain its existing6000-character projection, shared by guard records. Do not reuse scope text across freshness checks. Memoization must not hide new text.
bounded_work.references: After successful observe the strong node map equals unique offered controls union offered SELECT option nodes; no omitted/offscreen signature nodes. Maximum500 references is a conservative bound for250 distinct SELECT target actions. Detached current targets may remain until baseline replacement, since the map is bounded and identity must be checked without erasing the baseline.
bounded_work.counts: Instrument actual guard builds, unique scope reads, strong-reference count, offered target/action count, omitted count, scan/serialization time and UTF8 bytes. Keep metrics outside progress identity. Guard builds <=250; scope reads <=unique materialized scopes.
bounded_work.limits: DOM traversal and exact global signatures remain proportional to DOM size. Bound guard work and transfer honestly; do not claim constant total CPU/memory or a general latency speedup.

overflow.measurement: Measure TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(publicObservation)).byteLength inside Chrome, excluding optional screenshot. MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES=262144. Bound the entire returned observation, including metadata. Avoid a self-referential bytes field or remeasure after adding it. Never truncate meaningful labels/values to fit.
overflow.result: Return only a bounded typed snapshot_too_large envelope with counts/attempted byte count, and no executable actions/token. Invalidate old executable baseline/references on overflow; no stale-table fallback.
overflow.python: Browser.observe and Browser.fresh parse explicit overflow into SnapshotTooLarge with bounded diagnostic counts. It is terminal, never StalePage, never part of the observation retry loop. A SELECT overflow tag is known-before-input only; a missing/malformed dispatch reply remains uncertain.
overflow.agent: After GATE-LIMITS integrate with its shared terminal wrapper. Clear decision/pending text and mark the old page diagnostic/not fresh. Before-input overflow executes nothing; after-input observation overflow preserves exactly one already logged history entry and does not reissue input. Do not replenish counters or ask the model to continue.
overflow.entries: Handle constructor observation overflow with owned-tab cleanup; valid new_goal observation overflow must not leave the old goal executable. Invalid policy/goal validation remains atomic and precedes every read.
overflow.adapters: MCP final verification overflow must produce stopped/snapshot_too_large even after a provisional DONE, retain earlier page only as not-fresh diagnostics, and preserve uncertainty/history. Avoid a generic new-goal failure path that probes/reuses the tab and silently resumes. Inspector disables commands through stopped state and clears executable choice. Report readers accept legacy data without making it executable.

tests.native_matrix: Unchanged pages, within-viewport geometry motion, title/URL, relevant scope and unrelated visible text, safe offscreen form properties, omitted control mutation, scroll height, duplicate labels, select value/label/ownership/reorder/disabled state, cache recreation and identical-document navigation. Compare global and scoped baseline outcomes separately. Replay all accepted SELECT tests through schema2.
tests.overflow_matrix: Through actual observation adapter: setup, predict freshness, pre-input CLICK/SELECT, after one logged action, new_goal, MCP final verification and inspector. Assert terminal code, no executable stale state or subsequent helper/model/input/recovery, and correct retained history/attempt outcome.

measurement.safety: Use prepare --fixtures with the already reviewed owned proxy/profile/daemon lab, verify manifest before every native test, no paid models or external URLs, and close all recorded processes afterward.
measurement.references: Retain original E/baseline snapshot and the preserved SELECT-stage snapshot checkpoint. Compare original transport/work numbers and SELECT-stage semantic parity separately. Use different owned tabs for baseline/candidate scripts so one script cannot overwrite the other cache.
measurement.dense_fixtures: 250,1000,5000 actual visible small controls on a fixed grid (not ordinary vertical flow that leaves most controls offscreen), plus a shared6000-character form/scope context. Keep first6000 visible-text characters constant while mutating omitted controls to isolate progress. These canonical stress pages must return full capped evidence below262144 bytes, not merely overflow.
measurement.oversize_fixture: A separate long meaningful label/value fixture, including multibyte Unicode, deliberately exceeds262144 bytes and proves explicit terminal overflow without truncation. Strong-reference and guard assertions still apply.
measurement.sampling: Record every attempt, including warmups, exceptions and timeouts. Use declared alternating baseline/candidate order and a fixed sample count (for example3 warmups plus10 measured scans per fixture). Report raw samples and count/min/median/p95/max for browser scan/serialization and end-to-end observation separately, alongside bytes and work/reference counts.
measurement.comparison: Below-ceiling candidate offers the same canonical supported semantic actions as the reference, except approved policy/multiple-select differences and stronger SELECT descriptor validation. Compare stable fixture DOM identities rather than coincidentally equal numeric node IDs across separate tabs.
measurement.claims: Report observed native byte/work savings and measured distributions; do not generalize a speedup from synthetic DOM or byte reductions alone.
